Keep the controller powered and connected
Removing power while the controller installs can leave it unusable until it is reflashed with a programmer.
Choose a .bin or .hex file built for this controller.
Firmware for other hardware can destroy the controller. Only continue if you know this build fits it.

VESC firmware names its hardware inside the image; this file doesn\'t. Check where it came from before installing it.
I\'m sure this firmware is for %1$s

The file is empty or couldn\'t be read.

The bootloader installs uploaded firmware. Update it if a firmware update keeps coming back to the old version.
Every controller on the CAN bus
Connect directly to a controller with firmware 3.45 or later to update the whole bus.
Installing. The controller restarts; keep the power on.
If you installed a different version, the bootloader rejected the image or is missing. Upload the bootloader, then install again.
The connection closed while the controller restarts
Keep the power on for at least 10 seconds, then reconnect.
Keep the power on and wait. If the controller doesn\'t come back, check its LEDs; it may need a programmer.
The controller still runs its old firmware.
The firmware is not for this hardware.
Every controller on the bus must have the same hardware. Update them one at a time.
This controller\'s firmware can\'t update the whole bus.
The image doesn\'t fit the update area, even compressed.
The controller couldn\'t erase its flash. Make sure the motor is stopped.
The controller couldn\'t write its flash.
The saved upload doesn\'t belong to this firmware or this controller, so it can\'t be continued. Start the update again.
every controller on the CAN bus
The bootloader is written first. If that fails, nothing else is installed.
A different firmware version can reset the motor and app settings. Back them up first.
Firmware for other hardware can destroy the controller.
After the upload the controller restarts and installs, which takes up to a minute. Keep it powered until it answers again.
If the upload stops before the end, the controller keeps its current firmware.
Every controller relays the upload; only the one you are connected to confirms each step.
If this upload fails, don\'t install firmware until a bootloader upload has completed.
This firmware can\'t erase the bootloader first. If the controller already has one, it will be destroyed and firmware updates won\'t work any more.
%1$s closed the connection to install the update. It restarts by itself, which takes up to a minute. Keep it powered, then connect again to see the new version.
Tabs, CAN selection and Disconnect are locked until the upload ends. The old firmware keeps running until the controller installs the new one.
The controller is installing the update. Keep it powered; the connection closes and comes back by itself.
No connection to the firmware archive. These are the downloads saved on this phone.
No firmware for %1$s is offered. Choose a file instead.
Part of the archive couldn\'t be read, so older versions may be missing.
Removes the hardware\'s protective limits. Only install it if you know why.
The archive is served over plain HTTP, like VESC Tool\'s. The checks catch a wrong or damaged file, not one changed on the way.
Couldn\'t download the firmware. Check the connection and try again.
That image is for other hardware than this controller, so it was refused.
The download didn\'t pass the checks (size, hardware name) and was thrown away.
No notes for these versions. The changelog may not be online yet, or this is not an upgrade.
The changelog couldn\'t be loaded and none is saved on this phone.
The controller still runs its old firmware. It only installs a complete image whose CRC matches, so stopping here loses nothing.
The upload area is shared with the LispBM script and QML package, so those were erased when the upload started. Install them again afterwards.
Resume continues from the last chunk the controller confirmed and doesn\'t erase again.
Choose the same firmware again to resume it.
The controller doesn\'t answer after an update
Wait. Installing takes up to a minute and the controller doesn\'t answer meanwhile. Keep it powered.
Disconnect the battery, wait ten seconds, power it on and connect again, over USB if you can. Bluetooth drops more often during updates.
If it answers with the old version, the bootloader found the uploaded image damaged and kept the old firmware. Nothing is broken; update again.

Where the bootloader drives the LEDs, red blinks after an update mean: 3 image too large, 4 image empty, 5 CRC mismatch (the old firmware started). Eight red blinks: the application area couldn\'t be written, and a programmer is needed.

No answer at all usually means there is no application left, for example when power was lost while the bootloader rewrote it. VESC bootloaders can\'t receive firmware themselves. Hold BOOT0 high while powering on (some boards have a boot pad or button) to start the STM32\'s own USB bootloader, then write the .bin to 0x08000000 with STM32CubeProgrammer or dfu-util. VESC Express (ESP32) modules: hold BOOT while connecting USB and flash with esptool.

If the board has no boot pad, or the ROM bootloader doesn\'t answer, use an SWD programmer such as an ST-Link on the board\'s SWD pads, with the same addresses. Write the bootloader to 0x080E0000 too if you can.
The connection closed. Reconnecting to the controller; this can take a minute while it restarts. Keep it powered.
It polls the controller, which must be left alone while it writes flash. Stop the recording before updating firmware.
